findings.title: upsampled_count undercounts events without sample_weight
findings.body: upsampled_count computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/fallback to 1 for rows where sample_weight is NULL. Allowlisted projects can contain events predating client error sampling, events from SDKs that do not send error_sampling context, or otherwise unsampled events; for those rows sum() ignores NULLs, so a bucket containing only such events returns NULL/0 instead of its real count and mixed buckets silently undercount. The transform in error_upsampling.py applies this to every count() for allowlisted projects, so historical/normal error events disappear from charts. Use a per-row fallback such as coalesce(sample_weight, 1) before summing.

findings.title: Negated or quoted event.type:error incorrectly triggers upsampling
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring check for 'event.type:error' on the lowercased query string. A query such as '!event.type:error' (explicitly excluding errors, e.g. transaction/default events) contains that substring and returns True, as would the text inside a quoted title/message value. The endpoint then rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight), which does not exist/apply for those non-error events, producing wrong (likely zero/NULL) counts. The query needs to be parsed (or at minimum negation/quoting handled) rather than substring-matched, and spaced forms like 'event.type: error' are also missed by the current check.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset and request query, not the scoped query actually executed
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and query arguments that differ from the closure values during dashboard discover-split handling (e.g. split_dataset=discover, errors_only_query with '!event.type:transaction', transactions_only_query), but the eligibility call passes the outer 'dataset' and the helper reads request.GET['query'] instead of the 'query' argument. Consequently split error-only queries can fail to upsample while split transaction/other queries can be decided from the unrelated original request query, and the split has_errors/has_transactions comparisons can mix upsampled and non-upsampled results. Pass scoped_dataset and the effective query string into the decision.

findings.title: Cached allowlist eligibility can go stale and be inconsistent within one request
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from anywhere (option changes have no invalidation hook), so removing a project from the allowlist keeps upsampling its counts (and adding one delays it) with no bound tied to config changes. Additionally _get_event_stats re-evaluates this on every invocation, and the dashboard-split flow invokes it several times per request; a cache expiry mid-request can make the error, original, and transaction sub-queries disagree. Combined with hash() collisions between different project sets for the same organization, one set can also inherit another set's cached eligibility. Compute the decision once per request (or key the cache deterministically on the project IDs) instead of relying on an uninvalidated TTL cache.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public function for non-allowlisted projects
findings.body: Unlike neighbouring internal aggregates, the new SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' in discover.py is not marked private, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits it as a user-visible column string. Any user can therefore send yAxis=upsampled_count() directly for any project/dataset, bypassing the all-projects-allowlisted gate in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, and get sum(sample_weight) results (NULL/0 for projects without sampling) presented as legitimate counts. Mark the function private like the other internal-only aggregates so it can only be produced by the server-side rewrite.

findings.title: Stray subproject file committed at repository root
findings.body: This adds a file named 'sentry-repo' containing only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a', which looks like an accidental git submodule/gitlink artifact rather than intended source. It should be removed before merge to avoid confusing tooling and repository layout.

findings.title: No tests for the public eligibility entry point, caching, or mixed sample_weight data
findings.body: The new tests only cover the private helpers _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query (happy paths), _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and the column rewrite. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects itself — including its 60s cache behaviour, the errors-vs-discover dataset gate combined with allowlist state, negated queries like '!event.type:error', and events in allowlisted projects that have no sample_weight/client_sample_rate — is never exercised at the unit level, and the Snuba tests only store events that all carry client_sample_rate=0.1. These are exactly the paths where counts can silently become 0 or be wrongly upsampled, so regression coverage should be added before merging.
